items.title: Presentation by M/s. FMC India Pvt. Ltd. The representatives of applicant made a detailed presented on all the four issues related to the new molecule Tetflupyrolimet technical.
items.decision: After detailed deliberations it was decided as under: i) Purity: RC noted that CSF submitted by applicant is not yet accepted in USEPA and the molecule is not registered in the country of its origin i.e. USA. In view thereof, applicant may please comply with the recommendations of in-house group on “Establishment of minimum purity in India based on the registration of technical active ingredient by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA)” as accepted in 421st RC meeting vide agenda item 3.1. ii) Committee accepted the contention of applicant on DHODH and PFAS. iii) The RC decided that as per the decision of 421st RC a Standard Deviation tolerance limit shall be applicable to the 97% minimum purity applied by their parent company in USA. The minimum purity is arrived at 94.624% min. iv) Therefore, the RC decided that the purity of Tetflupyrolimet technical shall be 94.6% minimum plus impurities to make chemical composition 100.00%. v) It was also emphasised that all the data submitted by the applicant such as ATR & Shelf-Life etc shall be according to Tetflupyrolimet technical as 94.6% minimum. The sample under PRV shall also be conforming to the requirement of Tetflupyrolimet technical as 94.6% minimum. It was also decided that if, the applicant accepts the above said decision, then the applicant has to give in writing for accepting the above decision along-with revised Form-I, MOA, Product Specification in consonance of Tetflupyrolimet technical 94.6% minimum. The representatives of the applicant presented that Based on the weight of evidence approach, there was no evidence of adverse effects on immune system components in short-term (28- and 90-day) studies in rats, mice and dogs, or in long-term studies in rats and mice. These endpoints included WBC parameters, thymus weights, gross and histopathology of thymus, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. Further, applicant presented the interpretation (extract from EPA document Part158) as below: • Hemosiderin deposits of the spleen may occur secondary to hemorrhage or hemolysis that is unrelated to direct immunotoxicity. • Spleen congestion (passive accumulation of blood) may result from non-immune toxic effects such as hemolytic anemia or barbiturate euthanasia. • Extramedullary hematopoiesis of the spleen is commonly seen in rodents (particularly mice) in the absence of underlying disease and can be indicative of anemia/hemorrhage/hemolysis, systemic inflammation, splenic trauma/necrosis, decreased hematopoiesis by the bone marrow, and neoplasia. • Spleen histopathological changes in the absence of other lesion are unlikey to be specific indicator of immunotoxicity. Additionally, expected dietary exposure levels are very low with margin of exposure more than 10 million. Hence, Applicant concluded “In view of observation and sufficient scientific weight of evidence (WoE) to conclude that Tetflupyrolimet does not have potential for immunotoxicity.” RC further noted the below facts: 1. Tetflupyrolimet is first and only new mode of action (MOA-DHODH Inhibitor) herbicide being introduced in over 30 years. 2. Immunotoxicity study is the mandatory data requirement for 9(3)TI new molecule as per extant guidelines to assess the overall safety of human being. 3. Toxicology data on tetflupyrolimet is being extensively debated, assessed and has not been accepted in USEPA till date. RC was further apprised with “A Retrospective Analysis of the Immunotoxicity Study (OCSPP Test Guideline No. 870. 7800)” published by USEPA dated February, 2013 wherein below was opined: “Traditional subchronic and chronic rodent studies can provide some information on certain immunological endpoints such as hematology, lymphoid organ weights and histopathology. Nonetheless, EPA concluded in 2007 that these endpoints alone do not provide a full and integrated evaluation of immune function. Evaluating the potential of a chemical to adversely affect the immune system function is important because immune system suppression has been associated with increased incidences of diseases. Accordingly, that year the Agency revised the Part 158 Toxicology Data requirements to require a functional immunotoxicity study for all food and non-food use pesticides.” In view thereof, RC decided that member toxicologist Dr Umesh D. Surrangi may assess the requirement of immunotoxicity study, so that a final an appropriate decision may be taken, since he was not present in the meeting.

items.title: Presentation by M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd. In terms of the RC decision taken in its 468th RC meeting, at agenda item no. 10.2 in relation to representation of Non verification of registration certificate of M/s Meghmani Industries Ltd. Ahmedabad wherein
items.decision: RC decided to invite the applicant for presentation before the RC. The decision of the RC read as under: “RC perused the agenda and expressed its serious concern on the issue of possessing of forged/fake certificate of registration for Sulphur 80% WDG purported to be issued vide Registration No. CIR- 69,758/2005(254)-Sulphur (WDG-1125) from F. No. 1,372-F 9(4)/2005 by M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. The issue came to light when the company moved an application for the attestation of this certificate of registration and on being enquired about the genuineness of the same from available records at Sectt. of CIB&RC it was revealed that the above file no. doesn’t pertain to any such application for the grant of registration submitted by the M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. Further the CR records that the above registration was approved by the RC in its 254th meeting on the contrary no such approval was found in the entire MOM of 254th meeting. Prima-facie RC is of the view that M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad is utilizing the above-mentioned CR which apparently appears to be fake and forged and, in any event, couldn’t be presumed as genuine. Such type of illegal activities is to be checked at the threshold with exemplary punishments to the wrong doers. RC still is inclined to grant an opportunity to show cause M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad before taking any further view in the matter. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to call M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad to submit their point of view on the above aspect in the next RC.”. The applicant appeared before the RC along with their Learned Counsel Sh. Ashish Kothari Advocate, during the course of RC proceedings the applicant has submitted a presentation document which is taken on record. Mr. Kothari submits that the applicant is a leading group engaged in manufacture of agrochemicals for more than four decades and enjoy a good reputation between the farmers due to its quality products. He further submits that the applicant is a law-abiding company and is committed to ensure all regulatory compliances. Mr Kothari further submits that the captioned RC of Sulphur 80% WDG has been issued around twenty years back and that point of time the applications were used to be submitted in hard copy mode and the CRs are also received in physical hard copy form. He submits that the captioned CR bears the signature of the then Secretary CIB&RC and also contains the official stamp and therefore the applicant was using the same under the bona- fide belief that the same is genuine. Mr. Kothari also submits that since then several endorsement and certification have been sought by the applicant and the same were granted by the RC on several occasions and no question was raised as to the lack of genuineness of the said CR. He also refers Section 51, 52 and 78 of the Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 which inter-alia relates to the presumptions as to genuineness of the certified copies. However, on instructions, he fairly states that since the question has been raised about the lack of genuineness of the captioned CR., and in full bona-fides they are ready and willing to surrender the original CR to the RC, with a liberty to reapply of the registration of the same as per the applicable guidelines. Now after hearing the submissions, the RC deliberated upon the same and is of the considered view that any sort of illegality as and when detected is to be thrown out at any stage. Since the applicant had made a fair submission and is ready to surrender the original CR and therefore the RC is of the view that the submissions so advanced by Mr. Kothari the Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant deserves consideration. Accordingly, RC directs the applicant to submit an affidavit on NJSP to this effect duly sweared in accordance with law under the signatures of the authorized person not below the rank of the Director of the Company with the original CR along with the all-consequential original endorsements/certifications received by the applicant, to the Secretariat of CIB&RC with copy of the same duly endorsed to the respective State Director of Agriculture/s and duly acknowledged by them. Sr. Law Officer is also requested to verify the contents of the affidavit so submitted by the applicant in view of the submissions/statements made in the presentation document. RC makes it clear that if any such instance is found in future and/or comes to the notice of the RC, serious legal consequences shall entail.

items.title: Follow up agenda item no. 11.1 of the 466 and 468th RC meeting pertaining to the compilation of all the approved guidelines along with specific conditions.
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in detail and appreciated the efforts taken up by the expert committee for the compilation of guidelines approved by the Registration Committee (RC) in its various meetings. The Member Secretary to the Sub-Committee made a detailed presentation on the guidelines and methodology adopted in compiling and classification of RC on the basis of applications. The RC profusely appreciated the concerted and dedicated efforts made by the Sub-Committee in compiling and completing this mammoth task. The members deliberated the issue at length and asked Dr. Poonam Jasrotia for modification in the categorization of guidelines such as the guidelines for inclusion of molecules in Schedule and Setting of manufacturing facility shall be categorised under Category-I etc. The RC considered all suggestions given by the Sub-Committee and after detailed discussions some of the suggestions were accepted. After over all deliberations, the RC approved the compiled guidelines. The RC made it clear that the data generations for biopesticides & Botanicals shall be accepted from NABL approved laboratories. RC further directed the Secretary CIB&RC to incorporate the suggestions and issue the public notice along with the compiled guidelines and seek the comments and suggestions from the stakeholders within 30 days’ time and put up these compiled guidelines with the comments, if any received so to the next RC for appropriate action.

items.title: Templates/Proforma for the scrutiny of the applications of registration of pesticides in various category.
items.decision: The RC recalled its decision taken in the 468th RC meeting held on 12.01.2026 vide Agenda Item No. 3.2, wherein the draft templates developed by the Sectt. of CIB&RC for speedy examination of applications under various categories of registration within the stipulated time were approved for inviting comments/suggestions from stakeholders. The RC noted that, in compliance with its earlier decision, the Sectt. of CIB&RC issued a Public Notice dated 12.02.2026 inviting comments/suggestions from stakeholders on the draft templates. The RC further noted that meetings with stakeholders were held on 06.03.2026 and 08.05.2026, wherein the comments/suggestions received were deliberated and subsequently compiled for consideration by the RC. All the comments and suggestion given by the various Stake holders such Pesticides Associations, individual applicants etc have been incorporated in the template. The revised and corrected templates were deliberated in details in view of the regulatory requirements of Chemistry, Toxicology, Chemistry, Packaging and Bio-efficacy (Herbicide Unit) etc. The RC observed that some of the pages are missing in the template. The same was presented by the Secretary to the RC. After detailed perusal and deep discussion RC finalized the revised templates for implementation. The RC further decided that these templates shall be made integral part of the guidelines in the CROP portal, so that it becomes the mandatory requirement of submission by the applicant at the time of filling an application of registration. It was further decided that, once incorporated in the Crop Portal no application shall be accepted without information in the respective templates under all disciplines as per the approved guidelines. RC also further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public notice on the website and addressing to the Pesticides Associations; requesting to encourage their members to come forward and submit the information in template in an endeavour to grant of registration speedily. It was also expected that the existing applicant shall also be given an opportunity to join in this endeavour to expedite scrutiny and analysis of data, if they want the scrutiny of their files at fast pace. After detailed deliberations, the RC approved the templates. The revised and approved templates, in sync with the Guidelines, are annexed at Annexure 3.2.1, for implementation by the Sectt. of CIB&RC.

items.title: Consideration of an application of M/s Willowood Chemicals Ltd., for grant of registration of Haloxyfop-p-Methyl Technical 95.00 % w/w Min. for TI-(New Source) u/s 9(3) of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and noted that Haloxyfop-p-Methyl and Haloxyfop-R-Methyl Ester refer to the same highly effective, selective post- emergence racemic herbicide. The 'R' and 'P' denote its chemical configuration as the active enantiomer, making it twice as potent as the older, unresolved mixture of isomers. Haloxyfop molecules are chiral, meaning they can exist in two mirror-image forms: the R-enantiomer and the S-enantiomer. These specify the R-enantiomer, which is the biologically active form that actually kills weeds. The original herbicide was simply called haloxyfop-methyl, it was a 50/50 mix of both the active (R) and inactive (S) forms. Haloxyfop-p-methyl CAS no. is 72619-32-0 & Haloxyfop-R-methyl CAS no. is also 72619-32-0, hence synonyms. The MSDS of Haloxyfop-R-methyl is attached as annexure-6.71.1. The product is already registered in the name of Haloxyfop-R-Methyl Ester Technical 94% w/w min. u/s 9(3)-TI is registered in favour of M/s Dow AgroSciences India (P) Ltd vide agenda item 6.5 of 429th RC meeting held in June 2021 in the country. Since this applicant company and the source of import are different and the purity is more, therefore, Haloxyfop-p-Methyl Technical 95.00 % w/w Min. may be entertained for TI-(New Source) u/s 9(3), subject to submission of a satisfactory clarification why they shall not be issued the registration in the name of Haloxyfop-R-methyl technical. After affirmative submission of clarification of above concern raised by the RC, applicant has to submit information/documents as per extended guidelines approved in 468th & 470th RC meeting such as apostille /notarized copy of application form containing Chemical Composition submitted to the regulatory authority in the exporting country with a undertaking by the source that their source can be cancelled without any notice, if their Chemical Composition is found different from the registered one at the time of registration, and submission of the original hard-copy Affidavit / ICAMA / Consent (Apostilled/Legalized) with geo tagging of manufacturing source, whichever is applicable, if not already submitted.

items.title: Consideration of the request from M/s FIL Industries Private Limited for the endorsement of change of corporate office address from H-88, The South Mall, South Extension-1, New Delhi-110049 To Plot No. 23, Local Shopping Centre, Near Pushpa Bhawan, Madangir, New Delhi- 110062 in respect of 02 Nos. of Registration Certificates.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the applicant has applied for the endorsement for change of its office address and being a private limited company, a query was raised to provide the proof of change of company’s address from the ROC. In the response submitted by the applicant it was pointed out that there is no specific requirement under the Companies Act, 2013 for the filing of such a requirement in case of change in corporate office and such requirement only applies if the registered office address is changed. RC also observed that the applicant has not referred to any specific provision which may indicate as such. RC also further observed that such submission of proof is required under the RC guidelines/checklist which are statutory in nature and the same are required to be adhered to. RC feels that any change in any place, it shall be obvious that such changes may also be notified to the concerned Statutory Authorities. Even RC is also of the view that in order to satisfy itself any legal documents relevant to the matter may be asked to be submitted by the applicant in order to enable the RC to arrive at a subjective satisfaction before taking a final decision. The applicant had since submitted the utility bill for the premises requested to be endorsed and therefore RC feels that the request may be considered this time to avoid any delay and to facilitate the same. RC accordingly decided to approve the same subject to submission of an affidavit duly sweared in accordance with law as to the genuineness of the submissions made by the applicant with the copy of the same duly endorsed to the State Department of Agriculture to be verified by Sr. Law Officer.

items.title: Clarification regarding applicability of State Verification Letter for unfreezing of user accounts on CROP Portal in cases where no certificate has been obtained by the firm.
items.decision: The Committee deliberated upon the agenda in detail. After examination of the matter, the Committee observed that in cases where a firm/entity had merely created a user account on the CROP Portal but had not obtained any Certificate of Registration, Import Permit, RTT Permit, Free Sale Certificate, or any other approval/document from the Secretariat of CIB&RC, insistence on submission of a State Verification Letter issued by the Directorate of Agriculture may not be necessary for activation/unfreezing of the user account. However, the Committee emphasized that the existence and operational status of the firm/entity should be duly authenticated before activation of such accounts. Accordingly, the Committee decided that, in lieu of the State Verification Letter issued by the Directorate of Agriculture of the concerned State, the applicant firm/entity shall submit documentary proof issued by GST authorities or any other Government office/competent authority {Pollution Control Board, State Industrial Development Corporation/Industrial Area Development Authority, District Industries Centre (DIC), Directorate of Industries/Department of Industries or any other Central/State Government Department or statutory authority maintaining records of operational business establishments} which can authenticate that the business establishment/site is genuine, operational, and functional. The Committee further decided that such requests for activation/unfreezing of user accounts may be processed subject to completion of prescribed KYC requirements and submission of requisite documents as prescribed at the Secretariat level only. In all other cases, the decision taken by the RC in its 471st Meeting held on 16.04.2026 under Agenda Item No. 10.26 regarding mandatory submission of State Verification Letter shall continue to remain applicable.

items.title: Request submitted by M/s. Syngenta India Ltd. for the consideration of application for the registration of Thiamethoxam 12.6 % + Lambda cyhalothrin 9.5 % ZC for the control of House insect pests under label expansion category of the Insecticides Act, 1968
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in detail on the justification proffered by the applicant. The RC observed that the proposed product has already been registered for the control of insect pests in various agricultural crops and not for the control of House Hold (HH) insect pests. This issue was also discussed in the last RC meeting too for the requirement of data on Health Monitoring studies, which is not a requirement under agriculture usage. The above study is a mandatory requirement for grant of registration under HH category. This requirement is also applicable to the label expansion cases for HH category pesticides. The submission of the applicant that the proposed product was already approved for use in various crops like cotton, maize, groundnut, soybean, chilli, tea, tomato etc. is not tenable as the purpose and usage of the proposed formulation is not for use in agriculture and consequentially the purpose has been changed and therefore the said data is inherently required to ensure the safety of human beings. The RC further noted that the Protocol of conducting the Health Monitoring Studies has been proposed by the Sectt. of CIB&RC in the present RC meeting itemised at agenda 10.51 and the same has been approved specifying the parameters for its applicability on house hold (HH) products. The requirement of seeking approval of protocol on each occasion of HH has been dispensed with immediate effect. Therefore, the applicant may be communicated that the data on Health Monitoring Studies to be generated as per prevailing guidelines and submit the same alongwith their application in appropriate category. In the present matter RC observes that as the application has been submitted with incomplete data, thus the RC decided to close the application and suggest the applicant to apply afresh with all requisite data of HH category. The scrutiny comments of the concerned expert shall be considered during processing of the fresh application and only new study shall be scrutinized as and when submitted again.

items.title: Follow up action on Agenda Item No. 10.16 of 470th RC Meeting decision w.r.t Representation by PMFAI with a request for clarification regarding selling of Technical Grade pesticides and requirement of license to sell technical in states other than the state where the manufacturing plant located.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and taking into the account the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971, it becomes apparent that the Insecticides Act, 1968 was enacted to regulate import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution, and use of insecticides with a view to preventing risk to human beings, animals and the environment per se. RC also observes that the said legislation creates a centralized registration mechanism for insecticides; and decentralized licensing and concurrent enforcement of quality control mechanisms through Central and State authorities. RC also observes that registration granted under the Act is Pan-India in character. Section 9 of the Act provides for registration of insecticides by the Registration Committee constituted under the Act. Once an insecticide is registered under Section 9, such registration is not confined to any particular State. The registration so granted, permits manufacture and sale of the product throughout India subject to compliance with the Act and Rules. Accordingly, RC notes that the statutory focus is upon the registration of the product by the RC and licensing of the manufacturing premises/activity by the respective State Governments. A manufacturing license authorizes production from the licensed premises. Separate sale licenses may be required for dealers, retailers, distributors, or Stockists etc. operating from commercial premises in any State. However, such sale licensing requirements applicable to dealers or distributors etc. cannot be conflated with the manufacturer’s license. RC is of the view that if the manufacturer appoints distributors or depots in another State, the relevant entity handling sale/storage operations may require the appropriate sale license under the applicable regulatory framework. Nevertheless, the manufacturer himself is not required to obtain a fresh/separate manufacturing license /permission merely because the goods move inter-State. and therefore, a manufacturer holding a valid manufacturing license for its insecticide manufacturing unit in any one State is not required to obtain another manufacturing license/permission separately, merely for supplying or distributing its products in any other State. Accordingly, RC is of the considered view that a duly licensed manufacturer may lawfully supply its insecticide products across India, subject to compliance with applicable sale/distribution licensing requirements for downstream channels. RC observed that being a policy matter the concurrence of DA&FW is required and therefore the RC directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for consideration and concurrence before its implementation and issue of public notice to this effect.

items.title: Follow up action on the 470th RC decision at Agenda Item No. 10.15 w.r.t representation by Agrochemical Manufacturers Association of India, Gujarat on the issue of “marketed by” arrangements.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observe that although the RC had dealt similar issues in its 461st Meeting at Agenda Item No. 10.5 which reads as under: “Clarification on inclusion of marketing agency in manufacturing license and issuing NOC for additional factory address RC perused the communication received from the state department of Karnataka inter- alia asking for a clarification regarding the endorsement of marketing agencies. The state government has quoted rule 20 of the Insecticides Rule which they have submitted that any alteration in the label and leaflets requires permission from the Registration Committee. RC deliberated the agenda in light of the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 and observed that the grant of licenses for manufacture, sale, transport, distribution etc. lies in the domain of the respective State Governments and RC also observed that any consequential changes w.r.t. the change in the marketing agencies may be made by the state government after due satisfaction to them. Further, any provision of the Act does not preclude the State authorities to carry out such amendments which does not substantially impact the conditions of the CR. Furthermore, the Rule 20 provides that any alteration of any inscription or mark, made on the container, label or wrapper of any insecticide may be made at the instance, direction or permission of the Registration Committee. In view of this Registration Committee hence permits the endorsement of the marketing agencies by the state government under the title “Marketed by” of the label as prescribed under the Insecticides Rules after due satisfaction to them following the prescribed procedure and abiding to rest of the conditions approved by the RC for a pesticide. RC directed Secretariat of CIB&RC to communicate the same to concerned pesticides Associations.” RC notes that a communication had been received from DA&FW vide email communication dated 12.03.2026 forwarding a letter/representation dated 06.03.2026 from Bhartiya Kisan Union requesting the complete abolition of Marketed by system by Pesticides companies and providing quality pesticides to farmers. RC observes that a communication was sent by the Secretary, CIB&RC on 15.05.2026 to DA&FW apprising the 461st RC decision (Agenda 10.5) along with the fact that the issues are under examination in terms of 470th RC decision (Agenda 10.15) and the RC shall take a final appropriate view in the matter. Now therefore, RC proceeds to examine the permissibility of a Separate Marketing agency/company for Insecticides. It is gathered that as per common practice in India, one manufacturer may be manufacturing a particular product for several other companies under their respective brand names for marketing purposes. RC looked into the Statutory Framework under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971, which expressly contemplate a distinction between the manufacturer and the marketer/vendor of insecticide products. RC perused Rule 19 of the Insecticides Rules, 1971 (dealing with labelling requirements) which mandates that the label of every insecticide package must contain, among other particulars the name and address of the manufacturer; and the name of the marketer. RC observes that this dual-declaration requirement demonstrates that the regulatory scheme anticipates and permits marketing arrangements. Since the domain of licensing lies with the State Governments and therefore the focal point of satisfaction lies with the State w.r.t. the issues pertaining to marketing agencies. RC is of the view that the States should also ensure that the manufacturers and /or marketers should not escape from legal consequences in case of any violations committed under the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules 1971. RC, thus, recognizes that concept of marketing agencies is legaland permissible under the applicable statutory framework, provided all registration and licensing requirements under the Statute are duly complied with. RC is of the view that being a policy matter the guidance and concurrence of DA&FW is also required and therefore the RC directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for consideration and concurrence before its implementation.
